Galluzzo — Florence, Italy

🟡 Local-source safety assessment · 74 areas reviewed individually Methodology →

Relatively safer day Relatively safer night

In detail

Galluzzo, together with Gavinana, forms Quartiere 3, which multiple 2025 reports based on Fondazione Caponnetto data identify as by far the safest of Florence's five administrative districts — around 8 recorded microcrime episodes in six months, versus well over 400 in the historic centre. No specific incidents were found for Galluzzo itself. Sources checked: La Nazione, Fondazione Caponnetto six-month microcrime report (Quartiere 3: 8 episodes, safest area).

Frequently asked questions

Is Galluzzo safe?

Wandroz currently rates Galluzzo in Florence as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Florence during the day and relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Florence at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Florence publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Galluzzo safe at night?

At night, Galluzzo is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Florence. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Galluzzo a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Galluzzo's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Florence) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. Is there official crime data for Galluzzo?

Not an official government crime feed — Galluzzo's rating comes from Wandroz's own current local/national press and survey research for this specific area instead (see the note on this page for what was checked and the sources used). An absence of recent negative coverage is treated as inconclusive, not as proof the area is safe. If you live in or know Galluzzo well, you can suggest a correction using the link below.
